claim.title: Colorado local-context neuron
claim.lede: This neuron responds most strongly to Colorado-local context, especially Colorado’s Front Range news, sports, community services and public records. It activates when the surrounding prefix supplies Colorado place names, area codes, venues or institutions, and its output direction raises Colorado, Denver, Boulder, Colo and Broncos. Strong positive products are both large and coherent; negative products are weaker and more heterogeneous.
claim.one_paragraph: Across 100 million tokens, product is centered near zero (median -0.029; 99th percentile 1.20) but has a long positive tail to 322 and a shorter negative tail to -73.5. The strongest positive anchors (322, 316, 310, 304, 298) sit in Colorado Front Range text: Longmont event listings, Boulder County farms, Denver sports and C.R.S. district resolutions. The largest examples occur where gate and value are both strongly positive (for example 18.5 × 17.375 = 322), and token selectivity is concentrated on Denver (mean product 89.9), Colorado (87.0) and Boulder (74.7). A +1 product output projection raises “ Boulder” (+0.743), “ Colorado” (+0.729), “ Denver” (+0.722), “ Colo” (+0.652) and “ Broncos” (+0.528). The negative tail is split among Chinese Qinghai provincial news (to -73.5), Highcharts source code such as .data/.x (about -43), and non-Colorado civic or contact records (-40 to -46). Material limitation: negative product is not one opposing concept; moderate negatives are common in ordinary prose and are weak evidence.
claim.negative_pole: The negative pole is heterogeneous. The most negative anchor is -73.5 on “(” in a Chinese news dateline mentioning Xining (西宁), followed by Qinghai (青海), county/province (县/省) and newspaper (日报) anchors around -35 to -54. Another cluster is source code, especially .data/.x/.series references in a Highcharts script (about -43), and a third is non-Colorado civic or contact text such as Montana BLM telephone numbers and a North Dakota legislative report (-40 to -46). Thus negative product mostly indicates departure from the Colorado-local pattern rather than a well-defined anti-Colorado entity. Ordinary English prose also yields small negative values, which are weak evidence and often belong to the uncertain group.
claim.what_would_change_my_mind: Similar positive products from non-Colorado local news or sports would argue for a broader local-information feature; conversely, Colorado-only text that fails to activate would undercut the entity explanation. A single coherent negative category, instead of the observed Qinghai, code and other-state clusters, would replace the heterogeneous-negative account.

claim.title: Colorado local-contact neuron
claim.lede: This neuron responds most strongly to Colorado Front Range local context: event listings, venues, public records, community services and contact lines, especially at a place name or the boundary before a 303/720/970/719 telephone number. Its output direction promotes Colorado, Denver, Boulder, Colo, Broncos and related local tokens. The response is not exclusively Colorado: a smaller token-level component also fires on some non-Colorado place names, numeric boundaries and code fragments.
claim.one_paragraph: Across 100 million tokens, product is centered near zero (median -0.029; 99th percentile 1.20), with a long positive tail to 322 and a shorter negative tail to -73.5. The top natural anchors are Longmont event listings, Boulder County farms, Denver sports and C.R.S. district resolutions; at the strongest, gate and value are both large (18.5 × 17.375 = 322). Controlled comparisons support a Colorado-local component: city-plus-303 `call` products were 86.5–126.0 versus 8.75–22.5 for matched out-of-state cities; Colorado venues reached 90.5–144.0 versus 0.87–20.1; Colorado area codes reached 141–191 versus 2.25–11.1. A Colorado venue without a phone still reached 191 at ` Colorado`, and a bare `City offices, 303-` reached 149, so neither cue is strictly necessary. Qualifying this account, 43 of 105 blind-labelled source-code points were positive (maximum 43.25), `大连` averaged 66.9, and some high positive activations occur in Kyrgyz text, so a narrower token/place-boundary component coexists with the Colorado effect.
claim.negative_pole: The negative pole is heterogeneous and is best treated as a departure from the Colorado-local contact pattern, not an anti-Colorado concept. The corpus minimum is -73.5 on `(` at the end of a long Chinese news prefix reaching a Xining/Qinghai dateline; the Qinghai `日报` anchor reaches -54 and the blind Qinghai candidate -52.75, with `环`, `省` and `县` also negative. Qinghai templates gave minima -25.9 to -36.8, below matched Xinjiang, Gansu, Sichuan and Beijing controls (-5.8 to -0.3). Highcharts `.data`/`.x` (about -43.5) and Montana or North Dakota civic contact records (-45.75 and -40.5) form separate mechanisms, so code and non-Colorado records do not collapse into one semantic category.
claim.what_would_change_my_mind: Non-Colorado local news or sports that reliably match the Colorado positive magnitudes would argue for a general local-information feature; conversely, Colorado venues and contact lines that fail under controlled templates would undercut the local-context account. A single coherent semantic or upstream mechanism shared by Qinghai, code and civic negatives would replace the heterogeneous-negative explanation.

response_rules.name: Colorado Front Range local context
response_rules.description: The full prefix establishes a Colorado Front Range locality or Colorado institution through place names (Denver, Boulder, Longmont, Fort Collins, Aurora, Berthoud, Niwot, Minturn, Fruita), area codes 303/720, C.R.S. citations, district resolutions, or local venues. response_rules.name: Colorado sports teams and athletes
response_rules.description: The prefix is a Denver-area or Colorado sports report about the Broncos, Rockies, Nuggets, CU, or local high-school/college teams and athletes, and the anchor introduces a player, team, game, score, or other sports detail. Explicit Colorado wording is not required when team names or the sports context identify the Colorado connection.

response_rules.name: Qinghai and Tibetan-plateau provincial news
response_rules.description: The full prefix is Chinese-language provincial or local reporting centered on Qinghai, Xining, Yushu, Sanjiangyuan, or Tibetan-plateau counties and institutions. The anchor falls on an administrative or place token (青海, 西宁, 省, 县, 日报, 环, 站长) or an adjacent punctuation or number within that report.

response_rules.name: Source code and chart markup
response_rules.description: The prefix is dense source code or JavaScript/library markup, especially Highcharts-style property and method chains such as .data, .x, .series, and .point, or similar script fragments. The anchor is a property, method, syntax, digit, or whitespace token inside that code context.

response_rules.name: Non-Colorado civic and contact records
response_rules.description: The full prefix is a U.S. civic, regulatory, or contact-directory passage tied to a state or agency outside Colorado, such as North Dakota legislative material, Montana BLM or ARM notices, or California/Oroville services. The anchor is a telephone-number digit, statutory citation number, address, or contact field, and no Colorado locality is established.

response_rules.name: No visible cue
response_rules.description: The prefix is generic prose, academic or mathematical writing, an ambiguous multilingual passage, or a mixed context in which neither the Colorado-local pattern nor a coherent negative cue can be established. Weak negative values in ordinary text also belong here.
